findings.title: Renderer tests omit three of the seven AdoptionOutcome kinds
findings.description: The slice design's Technical Requirements specify `renderAdoptionFacts (every outcome, the state-set notice, "none found" facts, the squadron bullet)`. Task 8T enumerates only brownfield (capped), adoption-in-progress, `NOT_EVALUATED`, the state-set notice true/false, empty lists, history unknown, and the squadron bullet. `already-planned`, `adoption-closed` and `greenfield` outcome bullets have no renderer test — and Task 7T exercises those branches only in `decideOutcome`, not in rendering. The renderer's exhaustive `never`-checked switch (Task 8) is exactly the code an untested branch protects. Add one case per remaining outcome kind to Task 8T.

findings.title: No task verifies `context_build` returns the AdoptionError as an MCP error result
findings.description: The Functional Requirements state: "A guide without the profile or prompt: `cf build` exits non-zero with the `AdoptionError` message; `context_build` returns it as an error. The concept prompt is never produced." The `cf build` side is covered (walkthrough step 4 in Task 15) and the core rejection is covered (Task 9T, Task 12 fixture 12), but nothing covers the `context_build` tool handler surface: Task 10T's "stub throws AdoptionError → rejects" is the core integrator, Task 11's `contextTools.test.ts` additions assert only which `adoptionStateWrites` value reaches the mocked pipeline, and Task 13's parity test uses a healthy guide. The handler's existing catch-all does convert thrown errors to `errorResult`, so the behavior likely holds by construction — but the criterion names this path explicitly and no task asserts it. Add an `AdoptionError`-throwing case to the `contextTools.test.ts` steps in Task 11 (assert `isError: true` and the message).

findings.title: Sub-second NFR is deliberately covered by cap tests; no load-test tier applies
findings.description: D2 restates the sub-second performance NFR. The breakdown covers it with the cap tests in Task 3T (early exit at the line threshold, `AdoptionError` at `MAX_WALK_ENTRIES`), which is the verification the design itself prescribes ("Tests assert the caps, not timings"). I confirmed `tests/load/` is mandated only by `rules/python.md` (no matches in `typescript.md` or `testing.md`), and the design explicitly rejects a timing test, so adding one would contradict the parent slice. No CI load-gating task is needed because no load test exists. No action.

findings.title: `hasBuildManifest` is a dependency the tasks never consume
findings.description: The design lists `hasBuildManifest` among the reused 260 dependencies, but D5's fact list (source, history, docs, ADRs, rule files, CI) has no manifest fact and no task calls it (verified: only `setupCiOffer.ts` uses it in `src/`). This is a vestigial reference in the design, not a task gap — inventing a manifest use would be scope creep. Noting it so the reviewer doesn't read the absence as an omission; no action required in the breakdown.

findings.title: Commit markers are checkbox tasks rather than plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description: The ten commit markers (Task 2C … 15C) are checklist items instead of plain, non-checkbox `**Commit**:` lines. Their placement is correct: each follows a tested state (implementation + test task), none appears after every task, and none is deferred to the end. Placement is what matters functionally; the format deviation is cosmetic. Optional to normalize.
